newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar settles above 70 U.S. cents at close.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar settles above 70 U.S. cents at close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed above 70 U.S. cents on Tuesday for the first time since January as a buoyant Australian dollar propped it up.
Dealers said U.S. shorts scrambling to cover in thin trading overnight and this morning had sent the Kiwi up above 70 cents.
Direction is likely to depend on the Australian dollar where some consolidation is picked before it pushes higher. If that happens, it will take the Kiwi on for the ride, they said.
At 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) the Kiwi was at US$0.7017/24 from a 0.7004/11 opening. The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.70, unchanged from the opening.
Dealers said Treasurer Winston Peters' Budget Policy Statement had no impact on the currency market.
Peters announced less new spending for 1997/98 but more in 1999/00 and a largely unchanged programme over the three-year term of the coalition government.

Although Peters said he did not want a fiscal easing to put added pressure on the currency, economists noted the new government plans to ease fiscal policy by $5 billion over three years. -- Simon Louisson 64 4 4714 276
